title: Discovering Structurally Plausible and Interpretable Cognitive Models with Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.13561v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Computational cognitive modeling has traditionally relied on manual model construction, which is a time-intensive process that requires substantial domain expertise. Although recent LLM-based approaches have begun to automate model generation, they often prioritize predictive accuracy at the expense of structural plausibility and parameter identifiability. We introduce DisCo, an LLM-guided framework that discovers interpretable symbolic cognitive models through evolutionary search with two structural components: a Validator that filters structurally invalid models, and a Cleaner that promotes parameter identifiability by removing redundant parameters. Across three behavioral tasks, DisCo consistently discovers models that achieve performance competitive with task-specific baselines. translated_title: 利用大语言模型发现结构合理且可解释的认知模型
translated_abstract: 计算认知建模传统上依赖人工构建模型，这是一个耗时的过程，需要大量的领域专业知识。尽管近来基于大语言模型（LLM）的方法已经开始实现模型生成自动化，但它们往往以牺牲结构合理性和参数可辨识性为代价来优先追求预测准确性。我们提出了DisCo，这是一个由LLM引导的框架，通过进化搜索来发现可解释的符号化认知模型，该框架包含两个结构组件：一个验证器，用于过滤结构无效的模型；以及一个清理器，通过移除冗余参数来提升参数可辨识性。在三个行为任务中，DisCo持续发现性能与特定任务基线相当的模型。消融分析表明，验证器对于恢复具有心理学意义的结构至关重要。缺少该组件时，模型往往会违反基本的结构约束。
tldr: 本文提出DisCo框架，利用大语言模型结合进化搜索，通过验证器过滤结构无效模型、清理器去除冗余参数，自动发现结构合理、参数可辨识且可解释的认知模型，其性能可与特定任务的基线模型相媲美。
en_tdlr: DisCo is an LLM-guided evolutionary search framework that discovers interpretable symbolic cognitive models, using a Validator to filter structurally invalid models and a Cleaner to enhance parameter identifiability, achieving performance competitive with task-specific baselines.
